source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-90: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 90 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the hang as an observation, not proof of cause. Assumptions: the collective, tensor/message shapes, failing world sizes, placement, launcher, and software stack are reproducible; unknown platform facts must be measured. Record exact NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/container/launcher versions, node and GPU inventory, rank-to-device mapping and order, TP/PP/EP placement, topology, selected interface and NIC/NUMA affinity, MTU/routes, InfiniBand/RoCE transport mode, rendezvous endpoint, authorized firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and clock synchronization. Redact endpoints, tokens, and credentials.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 81: rank mapping or communicator ordering diverges when additional ranks join. Hold workload, versions, placement, message sizes, and timeout policy constant. Binary-search the minimum failing world size and repeat each condition at least three times. Collect synchronized per-rank logs with the last completed communicator phase/collective, rank mapping, selected transport, first-failure timestamp, timeout reason, and communicator-formation result. Gather topology and route/MTU snapshots, NIC/NUMA affinity, CPU/GPU utilization, memory and file-descriptor limits, and authorized port reachability. For InfiniBand/RoCE, capture link state, error/retransmit counters, congestion indicators, and relevant NIC counters with timestamps; do not infer causality from a single counter.

Use matched reduced-world baselines and a full-world baseline, changing one factor at a time: explicit rank mapping, interface/NIC affinity, transport choice where supported, and the suspect software/configuration or resource limit. Preserve a known-good configuration and stop if any trial risks production impact, exceeds the agreed timeout, shows data-integrity errors, or worsens error/retransmit rates. Roll back immediately to the known-good image/configuration and terminate/clean up the test job; verify all ranks exit and no stale processes or ports remain. Do not change firewall, routing, drivers, or fabric settings without authorized change control.

Report measured values with units (world size, communicator-init and collective latency in ms, timeout duration in s, bandwidth in GB/s, link rate, error/retransmit deltas, CPU/GPU/memory utilization, and trial counts), confidence intervals or run-to-run spread, and confounders such as placement, concurrent traffic, thermal throttling, clock skew, retries, and workload drift. Claim a diagnosis only when the hypothesized change reproduces the boundary and the matched control removes it; otherwise report unresolved alternatives. Evidence required before claiming improvement: raw redacted logs, exact configs and versions, rank/topology/NIC maps, repeated baseline-versus-change results, network counters, cleanup/rollback evidence, and approval/change records.
